title: chore(packages): publishing metadata for the 73 published packages — per-format types, sideEffects, publishConfig, and 18 missing READMEs

Part of #26095

Clause-②: no

#26095 asks for two things in order: one reading of publint and @arethetypeswrong over the 73 published packages outside `ui/`, then the repairs that reading names. This PR carries the reading, the manifest repairs and the 18 missing READMEs. The 14 LICENSE copies the card also asks for are 2,828 lines of byte-identical text on their own, which puts the two halves together over the 3,000-line threshold, so they land as a second PR off this branch once this one merges (that is why this body says `Part of`, not `Fixes`).

## The reading

publint 0.3.25 and @arethetypeswrong/cli 0.18.5, over all 73 non-private manifests under `packages/**` (none under `ui/`), each staged as `npm pack` would ship it — the manifest, the `files` whitelist, `README`/`LICENSE`/`CHANGELOG` and each `bin` target — on a fresh `origin/main` (`d1ea2363f`) build of every one of them. No gate is added for either tool; this is the one-time reading the card asks for.

## What was repaired

- **Types per module format** on 38 manifests. One `types` entry served both formats, so a TypeScript consumer importing the ESM build was handed the CJS declarations — every one of attw's 38 `FalseCJS`. Each `{types, import, require}` entry becomes `{import: {types, default}, require: {types, default}}`, pointing at the declaration file the same tsup run already emits for that format. No subpath is added or removed and no JavaScript target moves.
- **`sideEffects` on the 72 manifests that declared none** (only `@objectstack/spec` did), read per package rather than set in bulk, as the card requires. An AST pass over every published package's `src` listed the top-level statements that run on import — bare imports, expression statements, top-level control flow — and two packages do work on import that a consumer gets by importing alone, so they declare their entry files side-effectful instead of `false`: `@objectstack/service-cluster-redis` registers its `redis` cluster driver at module load ("importing this package is enough"), and `create-objectstack`'s bin reaches its program through a bare `import '../dist/index.js'`. Everything else is `false`: the remaining hits register into a registry in the same module that exports its readers (`formula`'s dialect engines, `objectql`'s ajv formats), build a process-wide store inside that module's own initialiser (`observability`), assert a constant at load (`types`), or act only when the file is the process entry (`cli`).
- **`publishConfig: { access: 'public' }`** on the 17 that had none, the value the other 56 declare.
- **`type`** on the 39 that shipped `.js` without declaring a format. Every `.js` under their `dist/` was read first and is CommonJS, which is what the absent field already meant. `@objectstack/console` and `@objectstack/skills` ship no JavaScript at all, so they stay unset and keep publint's suggestion.
- **`engines.node >= 22.0.0`** on the 22 that had no `engines`, and **`repository.url`** as the full `git+https://` git URL on 71 (two already spelled it that way).
- **A README for the 18 published packages that had none** — one paragraph of what the package is, the first import a reader writes, and a link to its docs page. These are the pages npm renders, and for these 18 npm rendered nothing.

## What is left, and why

- **`@objectstack/core` keeps its single `types` entry, so its two `FalseESM` stay open.** Its `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.cts` are two separate declarations of the same classes, `ObjectKernel`'s private `plugins` among them, so serving them per condition hands a consumer that reaches core through BOTH resolution modes two incompatible types. `@objectstack/plugin-dev` is that consumer: its `await import('@objectstack/objectql')` resolves with `resolution-mode: import` inside a CommonJS declaration build while its static core import resolves `require`. Measured with the split in place: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-dev build` fails `TS2345` at `src/dev-plugin.ts:523` with "Types have separate declarations of a private property 'plugins'"; without it, exit 0. The fix is core's dual build, not its export map.
- **`NoResolution` under `node10`, on the 15 packages with subpath exports.** TypeScript's legacy `node` resolution predates `exports` and cannot read a subpath from it at all. Every package here declares `engines.node >= 22.0.0`, and the alternative — a `typesVersions` map — is a second declaration of the same surface, drifting from `exports` the day either is edited. Left declared rather than mirrored.
- **`CJSResolvesToESM` on four subpaths** (`cli` `.`/`./console`/`./hook-body`, `create-objectstack/created-summary`, `metadata-core/testing`, `service-cluster/testing`): these are ESM-only entries, so a `require()` from CommonJS reaches ESM. Making them dual-format changes the export map's shape, which #26095 puts outside this card.
- **`FalseExportDefault` on `@objectstack/driver-memory`**: its `src/index.ts` ships an `export default` object whose CJS build lands as a `default` property. The repair is the package's own export surface, which this card does not touch.

The three classes above are reported to the seat as out-of-scope findings for cards of their own.

## Verification

- `turbo run build --force` over all 73 published packages at this head: **72 of 72 tasks successful** (73 packages, one with no build task). The `type` additions are the risk this run exists to answer — tsup picks output extensions off `type` — and the built file set is byte-for-byte the same list of names: **1,103 `dist` JS and declaration files before and after, `diff` clean.**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-dev build`: exit 0 at this head.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 95 families for this diff; the run record reconciles with `--ran` at **95 accounted, 94 run, 0 unrun**. Every one of the 94 exits 0. The one NOT MEASURED is `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`, which refuses its own prerequisite on a shallow clone (exit 3, its reserved code) because its positive-control fixture is pinned to a commit this checkout cannot reach; its real scan, `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs`, exits 0. `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` refuses the same way for the same reason and was re-run as its `--self-test`, which passes. CI has the full history.
- Gates worth naming for this diff, all exit 0: `check:published-files`, `check:published-readme-exports`, `check-published-readme-links.mjs`, `check:manifest-repository-directory`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lockstep-package-count`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`, `check:sdui-manifest` (the manifest re-records byte-identical).
- Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint` first among them) and the type-check lanes are CI's runs, not this branch's.

## Changeset

One `patch` in `.changeset/26095-publishing-metadata.md`, naming all 73 packages: every one of them ships a changed manifest, and 18 also ship a new README.
